name: recording usage and reading the totals back, on this machine, Nave
conditions: this machine and not a runner: 16 CPUs, with no service kept to a set of CPUs. Made-up usage events, each a customer, a model and a number of tokens, spread over 100 customers, are recorded and the totals read back, and the clock runs until the tool's own total of the tokens is right. Nave meters inside the gateway: one thread admits and settles 20,000 calls against keys, users, teams and an organization in memory. OpenMeter is its quickstart, with the sink's one-event commits dropped for its default batch of 500: one client sends 20,000 events in batches of 100 and asks its API for the totals. This race is here because OpenMeter never counted every event on a GitHub runner: in four runs there, on two CPUs and on all four, its sink logged that listing Kafka's topics timed out and stored between 2,945 and 19,870 of the 20,000 events
